notes:
This category was listed as not obtained until 2026-09-08. It rests on one shop and that shop is not in Japan: fashionnova.com, a US fast-fashion retailer, whose whole-catalogue verdict is suspect and whose values are recorded in whole ounces. Every line below comes from a slice of it that comes back usable on its own, with n >= 50 and a spread of at most 2.0. A t-shirt is the same object wherever it is sold, which is why this is worth having at all; a Japanese cut is not a US cut, which is why it is worth saying where it came from.

No second catalogue corroborates any of it. tentree.com publishes a band table (every tee 400 g), and the Japanese clothing shops that publish grams sell kimono and workwear, not the tees, hoodies and coats the live search returns. So there is no cross-shop check of the kind the food and fishing categories have.

There is no category average, because a t-shirt and a winter coat are four times apart. fallbackG is null.

Not obtained: dresses. The slice is real — n=3,578, median 431 g, spread 1.71 — but the Japanese word for one, ワンピース, is also the title of One Piece, and the live search returns One Piece manga, figures and cards by the hundred. A dictionary that matches one word at a time cannot hold that word, so the measurement is recorded here and not turned into a line.

Also not obtained: kimono and obi (the Japanese shops that carry them publish pseudo or under-threshold rows, see japan-clothing.com above), socks and underwear (14 rows), used and vintage grading of any of it (a 50s Levi's jacket and a new denim jacket are the same object to this table), and a Japan-based seller for anything here.

Three words in this category are inside longer words that name something else, and a dictionary that matches a substring cannot see the difference. The Japanese for coat is inside the Japanese for coating, so a bottle of coating agent would read as a 953 g coat; the Japanese for knit is inside the word for a knit cap, which is a fifth of the 408 g sweater; and the Japanese for hoodie is also how the pen brand Parker is written. None of the three appears in the dev half of data/weights-corpus.json today, so none of them is a measured misfire yet — they are the first things to gate in src/lib/pricing/weights.ts when this category is wired in.

The jeans line is men's jeans (the shop types them separately). The women's slice comes back suspect and sits at 635 g, so a women's pair reads about a quarter heavy on the 794 g line.
